Subject: Request: committed p95 <50ms for critical inference path

Hi Markus / Marissa,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. As mentioned, LumenArc is preparing to launch an inference-heavy feature for our consumer offering and latency is a hard requirement for the product to be viable. We ran a short baseline and attached the numbers — we're seeing median ~22ms but p95 spikes up to ~120ms under burst.

Ask: Can Redwood provide a written commitment for p95 <50ms for our production traffic (est. steady-state 120 qps, peak 300 qps) with an operational runbook and agreed fallbacks? We understand this likely needs dedicated resources or special routing; please propose options and rough commercial uplift.

Procurement contact: procurement@lumenarc.ai (CC'd on later threads)

Attachments: LumenArc_latency_report.csv

Best,
Ana Torres

Team — forwarding LumenArc's formal ask. Key points: they expect p95 <50ms, steady 120 qps, peaks to 300 qps. They attached a short latency report.

Questions I need by end of day Friday:
- Engineering feasibility: what architecture will guarantee sub-50ms p95? Dedicated GPU pool? On-prem/private?
- Ops constraints: what runbook & maintenance windows do we need to guarantee this SLA?
- Commercial: rough uplift % for dedicated capacity + priority routing + 24/7 support.

Thoughts so far: this sounds like a classic Dedicated + pinned model + aggressive caching scenario. We should also think about a conditional SLA (pilot -> full commitment). Please include any hard limits (model size, sequence length, quantization constraints).

Markus — quick technical readout after looking at their sample:
- With a Dedicated pool sized to sustain peak concurrency (we should target sustained 350 concurrent requests headroom), sub-50ms p95 is achievable for decoder-only models up to ~7B if we use NVidia H100 / A100 with 8-16 token batching and quantization to int8.
- KV cache warm-hit ratios and prefix caching are essential — the p95 problems correlate to cache cold starts and multi-tenant contention.
- If they have long contexts (>8k), latency will increase; we need the exact sequence length distribution.
- Throughput assumptions: 120 qps steady at avg seq 256 tokens -> roughly N GPU shards (I attached capacity_calc_A100.xlsx with a cost envelope).
- Ops: must pin model revision and allow only canary rollouts. No automatic model reloading during business hours; maintenance windows must be agreed and compensated with credits.

Risks: sudden traffic pattern shifts (fanout events) can break the p95; mitigation is burst capacity + autoscaling with warm standbys (costly).

I recommend we propose two paths:
A) Strict SLA option: Dedicated cluster, pinned model, 12-month minimum commit, prioritized support, and active prefix caching. Service credit schedule on miss.
B) Pilot option: 3-month pilot with Canary Dedicated pool + agreed SLO (soft target) to gather telemetry, then convert to A after telemetry pass.

Attaching: capacity_calc_A100.xlsx (capacity model + cost delta)

—David
Engineering — Runtime & Platform
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jan 2028 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: committed p95 <50ms for critical inference path

Markus / team — product/CS perspective:
- From a product risk point of view, we can offer a conditional SLA that ties the p95 target to a set of operational controls owned by the customer: locked model version, enforced prompt length limits, prefix caching behavior, and an agreed traffic shaping policy.
- We should require a 12-month committed spend for the strict SLA (this offsets the warm-standby cost). For customers unwilling to commit, we offer a time-bound pilot (6–12 weeks) with a best-effort SLO and an engineering playbook.
- Must-haves in the mutual action plan: runbook (detection & remediation steps), escalation matrix (SRE on-call), maintenance windows, telemetry dashboard access, and a breach credit table.

Proposed language for external:
"Redwood will provide a target p95 <50ms for the agreed traffic profile provided the customer adheres to the operational requirements and committed capacity. Exceptions related to third-party cloud region outages, model changes, or customer-driven traffic pattern shifts are excluded."

I'll draft the MAP and SLA language. Attaching the first-pass proposed_mutual_action_plan.pdf.

—Grace
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: LumenArc request — proposed commitment & runbook

Hi Ana — thanks for the clear brief. Attaching a proposed plan (Grace's MAP + David's capacity notes) and a link to a DocuSign wrapper for the commitment. High-level options:

1) Strict SLA (Recommended): 12-month committed capacity; Dedicated cluster; pinned model; SLA: p95 <50ms for the agreed traffic profile; service credit schedule for missed windows.
2) Pilot: 6–12 week pilot on a canary dedicated pool with operational playbook and telemetry access; after pilot we evaluate full SLA conversion.

Estimated commercial uplift: +60–95% over standard hosted pricing depending on shard sizing and warm standby needs (David's calc attached).

Next steps: please review the MAP, confirm whether you prefer the Strict SLA or Pilot, and have procurement confirm billing/PO cadence. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/s/abc123-LumenArc-MoU

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute ops deep-dive with David/Grace this week to lock down sequence-length assumptions and traffic shaping.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this quickly.

Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Markus / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the level of detail. We reviewed internally and want to proceed with a slightly modified approach:

- We prefer the Pilot -> Full conversion path, but would like the pilot to be 6 months (not 6–12 weeks) given the product launch timelines and to collect broader traffic variance.
- We agree to lock the model version and apply prompt length guidance. We also request a guaranteed fallback policy during maintenance windows (route to a cached lightweight model) so customer-facing experience has graceful degradation.
- Procurement will review the DocuSign wrapper; our procurement contact is julie.hernandez@lumenarc.ai. Procurement will push the SOW and PO details within 48 business hours after we confirm the pilot terms.

Attached: signed_MoU.pdf (this is a signed acknowledgement of the MAP; final DocuSign to follow once procurement signoff).

Can we schedule the ops deep-dive next Wednesday? Please include David and Grace.

Best,
Ana Torres
